note: Profiles are cumulative: moderate = light + its own list; super = moderate + its own list. Every entry names the reason it is there. microsoft_disposition, when present, is Microsoft's own word for that exact service name, harvested by READ-ONLY-verification/Harvest-ServiceGuidance.py.

Screen capture for Store apps - and the Snipping Tool IS a Store app. Disabling it silently breaks Win+Shift+S, the screenshot shortcut, with no error message: the overlay simply never appears. Confirmed on this machine on 2026-08-27 after the SUPER profile was applied. Its own description ('capture service for screen capture in Store apps') is accurate and badly undersells what depends on it.

Bluetooth Support Service - has an honest switch: the owner toggles Bluetooth from the quick menu day by day and Windows honors that switch. Killing the service kills the switch: the menu says On and nothing underneath can start, exactly the camera-slider failure. Radios are present on this machine (DEC-06-016).
Bluetooth Audio Gateway - same ruling as bthserv: the quick-menu toggle is the control, the profile is not (DEC-06-016).
Bluetooth per-user service - same ruling as bthserv (DEC-06-016).

Mobile hotspot - the owner turns the hotspot on and off from the menu as the day requires; the capability must exist for that switch to mean anything. Profiles target what IGNORES the user's switch, not what honors it (DEC-06-016).
Internet Connection Sharing - the hotspot's plumbing; same ruling as icssvc (DEC-06-016).

lockoutRisk.reason: Kerberos Local Key Distribution Center. Microsoft's own description: 'This service enables users to log on to the local machine using the Kerberos authentication protocol. If this service is stopped, users will be unable to log on to the local machine.' Build 26200 is the train moving local authentication off NTLM onto this. It was in the MODERATE profile.
Windows Hello container; same lockout risk as NgcSvc.
Windows Hello / PIN. This machine has NgcSvc RUNNING - a PIN is very likely in use. Disabling it can leave you unable to sign in.
Credential Manager; saved credentials and some sign-in paths.
Microsoft Account sign-in assistant. This is the RECOVERY path for a forgotten PIN at the logon screen - protecting NgcSvc and disabling this is internally inconsistent.

Windows Camera Frame Server. Disabling it ends camera access for every application - but the reason it is on THIS list rather than in a profile is sign-in: Windows Hello FACE uses the infrared camera, and that path runs through FrameServer. Confirmed on this machine 2026-08-27: with the service disabled, face sign-in did not work; with it restored, the Biometrics log records the Facial Recognition sensor creating a Biometric Unit and the Windows Biometric Service authorising the user. A machine whose owner has only face enrolled would lose their sign-in method with no error explaining why. Excluded from every profile.
Health watchdog for FrameServer. Moves with it - disabling one without the other achieves nothing, and FrameServer is a sign-in path.

Diagnostic Policy Service. The supervisor of Windows' self-diagnosis: decides which of 54 registered scenarios run and dispatches them to the two Wdi hosts. Automatic, LocalService, no start trigger. Nothing declares a dependency on it. Disabling it also stops boot and shutdown performance logging outright [R-113]. Treat as one unit with WdiServiceHost and WdiSystemHost - see BLAST-RADIUS-diagnostics.md and DEC-06-010.
services.microsoft_disposition: VDI optimisation guidance lists it among services that may be considered to disable [R-110]; cost stated as 'Disabling this service disables the ability to run Windows diagnostics.' [R-111]. Server services guidance: No guidance.

services.reason: Diagnostic Service Host - wdi.dll hosted at LocalService privilege, the container DPS loads diagnostic modules into [R-108]. Named in Microsoft's Windows Filtering Platform documentation as a principal granted rights on WFP objects alongside the firewall and IPsec policy agent [R-116], which is how network diagnostics reach firewall filters. A component of DPS, so covered by Microsoft's own caveat [R-114] - see BLAST-RADIUS-diagnostics.md and DEC-06-010.
services.microsoft_disposition: Absent from the VDI table and No guidance in the server services guidance. The absence carries no signal: the VDI table states it omits already-Manual services [R-115], yet lists WdiSystemHost, which is also Manual.

services.reason: Diagnostic System Host - the SAME binary as WdiServiceHost (wdi.dll), hosted at LocalSystem instead [R-109]. Running on this machine at the time of measurement. Loads any of 29 registered diagnostic modules resolving to 15 DLLs. A component of DPS, so covered by Microsoft's own caveat [R-114] - see BLAST-RADIUS-diagnostics.md and DEC-06-010.
services.microsoft_disposition: VDI optimisation guidance lists it among services that may be considered to disable [R-110]; cost stated as 'Disabling this service disables the ability to run Windows diagnostics' [R-112]. Server services guidance: No guidance.
